items.topic: Artifact launch model — how callers provide apps to the emulator
items.context: Currently findArtifact() discovers built Electron apps by looking at scenarios/{scenarioName}/platforms/electron/dist-electron. After extraction, the emulator can't have cross-scenario filesystem knowledge. The API needs a launch contract. Three approaches: (1) callers always provide an explicit app_path, (2) callers provide a scenario name and the emulator uses a discovery endpoint, or (3) callers upload/register artifacts with the emulator.

options.label: Explicit app_path required — callers resolve artifacts before calling emulator
options.rationale: Simplest contract. Emulator stays generic — it launches whatever binary it's given. scenario-to-desktop and smoketest already know where their artifacts are. Keeps artifact discovery logic in the scenario that owns the build pipeline.

options.label: Scenario-name discovery — emulator resolves artifacts via vrooli CLI or filesystem convention
options.rationale: Callers just say 'launch scenario X'. More convenient but couples the emulator to Vrooli's scenario layout conventions. Breaks if conventions change.

options.label: Artifact registry — callers register artifacts with the emulator, then reference by ID
options.rationale: Most decoupled, supports remote artifacts and versioning. But adds a registration step and storage management that may be over-engineered for local-first operation.

items.topic: Captures ownership split between emulator and scenario-to-desktop
items.context: The captures system has two roles: (1) creating captures (screenshots/recordings from display sessions) and (2) persisting/browsing captures (metadata store, file management, listing endpoints). Currently both live in scenario-to-desktop. The emulator will own display sessions, so capture creation naturally moves with it. The question is where persistent capture management lives.

options.label: Emulator owns creation + temp storage; consumers own persistence
options.rationale: Emulator provides screenshot/record actions that return temp files or streams. Each consumer (scenario-to-desktop, deployment-manager) persists captures into its own store. Emulator stays stateless for captures.

options.label: Emulator owns the full captures lifecycle (creation, persistence, browsing)
options.rationale: Centralizes all capture management. Consumers query the emulator for capture history. But this makes the emulator a storage service, not just a display service.

items.context: Based on the round 1 decision (B with headless-ready API), the extraction needs phasing. The question is what the minimum viable phase 1 delivers. The livedesktop package, procmetrics, and platform backend are all extraction-ready. Smoketest migration adds complexity but was committed to. The iframe UI pattern is well-understood from app-monitor/deployment-manager.

options.label: Phase 1: API + headless sessions + VNC proxy. Phase 2: UI + iframe embed. Phase 3: smoketest migration.
options.rationale: Backend-first approach. Gets the service contract stable before adding UI complexity. Smoketest last because it requires the most coordination.

options.label: Phase 1: API + UI + iframe embed. Phase 2: smoketest migration.
options.rationale: Two phases instead of three. Ships a complete user-facing product in phase 1. More initial work but fewer integration points to manage.

options.label: Single phase — extract everything at once
options.rationale: No phasing overhead but highest risk. All-or-nothing delivery.

items.text: The full livedesktop API surface is 11 HTTP endpoints + 1 WebSocket: session CRUD (create/list/get/delete), heartbeat, launch, artifact discovery, control actions, metrics, file serving, and VNC proxy. Control actions include: launch_app, quit_app, screenshot, start_recording, stop_recording, offline_mode, slow_connection, inject_env, resize_display, clipboard_read, clipboard_write, dark_mode, and locale. This is a mature, well-defined API that can transfer to the emulator nearly unchanged — only the route prefix needs updating.

The iframe embed pattern is well-established in the codebase. deployment-manager fetches an external URL from a backend endpoint (GET /embedded/{name}/external-url) and renders it in an iframe with query params for context. app-monitor uses @vrooli/iframe-bridge for parent-child communication with recursive embedding protection (max depth = 1). The emulator UI should follow this pattern: expose an /embedded/emulator/external-url endpoint, support query params (session_id, display config), and integrate iframe-bridge for bidirectional events.

procmetrics is fully self-contained — it reads /proc/{pid}/* files and uses X11 tools (xdotool) for window detection. Interfaces: Monitor (Start/Stop/Report/Done), MonitorFactory, ProcReader, WindowDetector. It tracks startup timing (launch → splash → ready), periodic CPU/RSS/thread samples, and produces summary aggregates. Migration feasibility is HIGH — it can move to the emulator with zero changes, or become a shared library if other scenarios need process monitoring.

Smoketest's display management is a thin wrapper: RequiresHeadlessWrapper() checks for DISPLAY env var, and if absent, prefixes the command with 'xvfb-run -a'. To delegate to the emulator: (1) call emulator to create a headless session (no VNC needed), (2) get the DISPLAY value back (e.g., ':100'), (3) pass it as env var to the test command. The emulator API already supports this — StartSession creates an Xvfb display and returns connection info. The headless flag just skips VNC/websockify setup.

The captures integration uses an optional dependency pattern: livedesktopService.WithCaptures(capturesService) wires it in, and screenshot/recording actions gracefully degrade if captures is nil (falling back to session-scoped temp files). This pattern should be preserved in the emulator — captures persistence is an optional consumer-provided callback, not a core emulator concern.
